correctness.rationale: The exact circumcircle parametrization with Jacobian 2ar³ turns the CDF into a translation-erosion integral. For fixed positively curved C² K the tubular signed-normal expansion of K⊖rT has an O_K(r²) remainder uniform over T in the unit disk. Two exact gap integrations give E[a]=3/(2π) and E[a p]=64/(3π²). Cauchy rotation averaging gives angular coefficients 24π² and 512P/3; radial integration proves t⁴ coefficient 6π²/A² and t⁵ coefficient −512P/(15 A³), with O_K(t⁶). All assumptions, normalization, measure-zero collinear cases, and non-contained circumcircle cases are handled. Embedded SymPy verifier reproduces both moment integrals and a Jacobian instance. Finite tests are not used to establish infinite scope.

originality.rationale: The 2026 primary full text computes the upper circumradius tail for the unit disk only, while the 2018 conditional law excludes circles protruding beyond the body, which affect the perimeter term. Searches for the lower tail, complete asymptotics, database constants, and implicit stronger results yielded no inspected claim determining both coefficients for arbitrary smoothly curved planar convex bodies. The result is not a restatement of a stronger inspected result. Some unindexed integral-geometric derivation remains possible.
residual_risks: A differently named unindexed integral-geometric calculation could already imply both coefficients.
The related February 2026 contained-circle note was inaccessible in full; its indexed stated event is not the one studied here.

value.rationale: The expansion recovers both planar intrinsic volumes, area and perimeter, from a single natural random-triangle circumradius statistic and gives the first nontrivial small-scale isoperimetric comparison. The universal angular mixed area–perimeter moment explains the shape-independence of the coefficients and supplies a reusable stochastic-geometric mechanism; it is neither a renaming of an existing exact CDF nor an arbitrary finite constant.
